core_technique: Anti-diagonal (wavefront) Needleman-Wunsch: three rolling int16 anti-diagonal buffers (d-2, d-1 -> d) computed with SSE2/AVX2/AVX-512 max/add intrinsics, plus a score-bound-derived band and a scalar two-row DP fallback for small/large n.
Score-bound-derived banded Needleman-Wunsch two-row DP, vectorised with AVX2 using an offset coordinate (G = H + 2j) so the left-gap dependency becomes a running/log-shift prefix maximum.

Banded Needleman-Wunsch: a main-diagonal match count yields a score lower bound that certifies a band width W, then the band is filled by full DP — an AVX2 anti-diagonal (wavefront) int16 kernel with an int32 scalar row-DP fallback.

Banded Needleman-Wunsch computed along anti-diagonals in int16 with AVX2 (plus an O(n)-memory exact two-row NW fallback), where the band half-width is derived from a score lower bound obtained by max-over-shift diagonal match counting.

Banded Needleman–Wunsch DP (scalar rolling band, plus an AVX2 anti-diagonal wavefront in 16-bit lanes) with the band width W derived from a lower bound obtained by scoring a handful of single-shift Hamming comparisons.

A near-verbatim xxHash64: four interleaved 64-bit lanes of add-multiply-rotate-multiply rounds over 32-byte stripes (unrolled to 64 bytes with prefetch), rotate-and-sum lane convergence plus asymmetric merge rounds, length addition, 8/4/1-byte tail folding, and a standard xor-shift/multiply final avalanche.

xxHash64: four parallel 64-bit accumulator lanes running the standard round (acc += in*P2; rotl 31; acc *= P1) over 32-byte stripes, merged by rotate-sum plus per-lane merge rounds, with a length-mixed tail (8/4/1-byte steps) and a splitmix-style xor-shift/multiply finalizer.

xxHash-style block hash: four parallel 64-bit lanes absorbing 32-byte stripes through a fixed number of ARX (add-rotate-xor) rounds with cross-lane pairing, then cross-fold merge, byte-tail loop, and a SplitMix64 multiply-xor-shift finalizer.

xxHash3-style hashing: 8×64-bit accumulator lanes over 64-byte stripes with 32×32→64 multiply-accumulate plus lane-swapped (acc[j^1]) data addition, a periodic xor-shift/xor-secret/multiply scramble every 16 stripes, length-seeded short-input regimes, and a 128-bit fold plus moremur xor-shift-multiply finalizer.

Chained CRC accumulation over 8-byte words (hardware CRC32C/CRC32D intrinsic, else a table-driven reflected CRC-64/XZ) with non-zero init constants and 2-3 interleaved lanes, length mixed in, finished by a fixed 7-stage xor-rotate/multiply/xor-shift avalanche finalizer (nasam head + rrmxmx tail).

Dijkstra's algorithm over a CSR adjacency, selecting the minimum by a SIMD/linear scan over a compact array of reached-but-unsettled nodes (array-scan variant with O(1) in-place decrease-key), with a work-budget/regime switch to a standard binary-heap Dijkstra.

Dijkstra's algorithm over a CSR adjacency, with a compact unordered array of active tentative labels scanned by an AVX2 argmin for extract-min plus O(1) positional decrease-key, falling back to a lazy-deletion 4-ary binary heap once the frontier exceeds a computed threshold; sink vertices are pruned from the frontier.

Frontier/round-based Bellman-Ford–Moore (SPFA-style level-synchronous relaxation over CSR with per-round stamp dedup), with a work-budget bail-out to binary-heap Dijkstra or O(n^2) array-scan Dijkstra by density

Delta-stepping: distance/delta bucket (drawer) queue with per-vertex CSR split into light (<delta, drained within the current bucket until fixpoint) and heavy (deferred to bucket end) edges, no priority queue and no settled test — with a plain O(n^2) array-scan Dijkstra used only for small (n<=256) or dense (m >= 0.1n^2) graphs and as an allocation-failure fallback.

Dijkstra's algorithm with a cost-model-selected backend: a lazy-deletion 4-ary binary heap for sparse graphs, or a dense O(n^2) linear array scan (AVX2-vectorised min-find with swap-with-last compaction) for dense/small graphs.

Anti-diagonal (wavefront) Needleman-Wunsch: each k = i+j anti-diagonal computed from the two previous ones in three rotating buffers, vectorized with AVX2 (int16 with a 32-bit fallback above the range guard) using a reversed copy of b so the diagonal's symbol pairs are contiguous, plus a scalar small-n path.

Exact Needleman-Wunsch computed by an anti-diagonal (wavefront) sweep with three rolling diagonals, SIMD-vectorized in 16-bit lanes (AVX2/AVX-512) with a reversed second sequence, plus 32-bit and scalar row-DP fallbacks — a standard diagonal-major vectorization of the textbook O(n^2) DP.

Banded Needleman-Wunsch with an AVX2 anti-diagonal wavefront, where an O(n) prefix-sum scan over all ≤1-gap alignments supplies a lower bound that (via score ≤ n − 5g) bounds the band width and occasionally proves the answer outright.

Banded Needleman–Wunsch DP swept along anti-diagonals with AVX2 int16/int32 lanes, where the band half-width W = floor((n-L)/5) is derived from a lower bound L obtained by the native's O(n) single-slip trial enumeration; the exact answer comes from the banded DP, not from the trials.

wyhash/xxHash-style block hash: four parallel 64-bit lanes of 128-bit multiply-with-hi^lo-fold over 64-byte blocks, rotate-and-merge, 16-byte and overlapping-tail folds, then a length-keyed multiply-xorshift avalanche finalizer.

FNV-1a-style xor-then-odd-multiply accumulation (`s = (s ^ byte) * M`) run over four independent 64-bit lanes for ILP, with a once-per-64-byte cross-lane rotate-xor, length folding, and a moremur-style 64-bit finalizer.

Multiply-free rotating hash: per byte, add into a single 64-bit accumulator then rotate left by a fixed odd constant (11), 8x-unrolled, followed by Thomas Wang's shift/add/xor 64-bit finalizer on the final state.

xxH3/xxHash-style multi-lane (8×64-bit) multiply–rotate–xor absorption of 64-byte stripes with block-index-derived key material (blk*PHI, blk0 seeding) so chunk position enters as data rather than as a serial chain, a ChaCha-like transpose/add-rotate-xor/multiply permutation for cross-lane diffusion, a splitmix64-style finalizer, and a fixed-chunk OpenMP commutative (+) reduction for thread-count-independent parallelism.

Byte-at-a-time single-accumulator fold (s = rotl(s,23) + b*odd_const + const), 8x loop-unrolled above 32 bytes, followed by a 7-round multiply/xor-shift (Murmur/splitmix-style) finalizer — i.e. the standard FNV-1a/xxHash one-accumulator mixing scheme plus a textbook finalizer; no avalanche test present.

Delta-stepping SSSP: bucket/bag ring of distance bands (delta = mean edge weight) with re-relaxation of tentative nodes, optional OpenMP CAS-min relaxation, plus work-limit bailout and guard conditions handing off to a lazy 4-ary-heap Dijkstra (which is also the small/degenerate-graph path).

Dijkstra with CSR adjacency and a compact swap-removal frontier array whose minimum is chosen each round by an exhaustive (AVX2/OpenMP) linear argmin with O(1) in-place label update — i.e. the classic heapless array-scan Dijkstra — plus a work-budget guard that switches to a 4-ary lazy-deletion binary heap.

Frontier-based synchronous-round Bellman-Ford/SPFA over a CSR graph, with per-vertex atomic CAS min-relaxation, an in-queue bitmask frontier, and OpenMP persistent-team barriers plus a serial small-frontier path — no priority queue or global argmin.

Dial-style bucket/monotone-clock Dijkstra: a circular array of nb distance-quantized buckets (width delta from weight statistics) with doubly-linked vertex lists, a 64-bit-word bitmap ctz scan to skip empty buckets, decrease-key by bucket re-insertion, plus a pop-budget guard that falls back to lazy binary-heap Dijkstra.

Dijkstra whose priority queue is a fixed-slot, position-is-identity lattice-of-lattices — an 8-ary hierarchical min-tree (SIMD qmin8) layered over dist[] with a settled bitmask, giving O(log_8 n) extract-min and decrease-key with no key migration or duplicate entries, plus an O(n^2) plain-scan path for n<=192.

Anti-diagonal (wavefront) Needleman-Wunsch with three rolling diagonal buffers, one sequence pre-reversed, AVX2-vectorized across each anti-diagonal in int32 or saturating int16 lanes, computed in a min-cost gauge E=(i+j)-2H and converted back at the end.

Standard global Needleman-Wunsch DP (+1/-1/-2) computed in anti-diagonal wavefront order with three rolling int16 diagonals and AVX2 16-lane max updates, plus a scalar 32-bit row-major fallback for large n.

Anti-diagonal SIMD (AVX2) Needleman-Wunsch with a 3-row rolling buffer, restricted to a band whose half-width is derived from a greedy/narrow-sweep score lower bound via the standard score-bound certificate (n - 5*w <= lb), with scalar full-DP fallback — i.e. classic banded/vectorised NW (KSW2/Ukkonen style).

O(n) prefix-sum enumeration of the ungapped diagonal match count plus every single-shift (one-gap-at-a-mismatch) alignment in both directions, taking the maximum via a SUNK sentinel and converting match counts to +1/-1/-2 alignment score — not a DP table.

Banded anti-diagonal Needleman-Wunsch DP (AVX2-vectorised, 3 rotating diagonals) whose band width W is seeded by a cheap single-gap prefix/suffix scan used only as an upper bound on the optimal score.

Single-pass byte-at-a-time chained rotate-add/xor-multiply mixer (rotation count driven by popcount of the byte) feeding four parallel accumulators, closed with a Murmur3-style fmix64 finalizer — i.e. FNV/xxHash-style multiply-xor-shift accumulation, with the four-beak agreement test inert (the all-nonzero check essentially never fails) and the 'discard' step a no-op wipe of dead locals.
FNV-1a-style byte-at-a-time hash: state = rotl64((state ^ byte) * 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15, 16) from the FNV offset-basis seed, 8x-unrolled, returning the raw state with no finalizer.

FNV-1a/xxHash-style streaming hash: one 64-bit accumulator, per byte xor-in then a fixed number of multiply-by-odd-constant / xor-shift-32 / rotate-27 mixing rounds, plus a length-mixing finalization returning the last xor-shift value.

Per-8-byte-block compression of a 64-bit state treated as an 8x8 bit matrix: 10 fixed rounds of XOR-in-message, 90-degree bit-matrix rotation (bswap + bit-transpose, or GFNI affine), carry-propagating corner-fold via 16-bit adds, then Davies-Meyer-style feed-forward addition of the pre-round state — chained Merkle-Damgard-style over length-padded blocks; no multiply-xor-shift accumulator.

Byte-at-a-time serial accumulator hash (xor byte, multiply by odd 64-bit constant, rotate) seeded with 2^64/phi, length-appended, then a 7-round xor-shift-multiply finalizer — i.e. FNV-1a/xxHash-style single-accumulator folding with a Murmur3-style avalanche tail.

Standard single-source Dijkstra on a CSR-built directed graph using a 4-ary min-heap with in-place decrease-key, plus generic micro-optimisations (cache-line-aligned heap, prefetching, interleaved edge payload) and an inert dead-code back-walk.

Dijkstra's algorithm over a CSR graph with a linear (AVX2/OpenMP-vectorised) array scan extract-min over a swap-compacted active set — i.e. the classic O(n^2) no-heap Dijkstra variant, plus a cheap predecessor-chain re-sum sanity check that is a no-op in practice.

Synchronous (Jacobi/double-buffered) Bellman-Ford: repeated whole-graph relaxation implemented as a per-node min-reduction over incoming CSR edges, reading only pre-round distances and writing a shadow array, looping until a round changes nothing or n-1 rounds elapse, OpenMP-parallelised.

Dijkstra's algorithm over a CSR adjacency structure with an unordered frontier array whose minimum is found by a blocked (64-entry) block-minimum cache and AVX2/SIMD linear min-and-find scans instead of a binary heap.

Dijkstra's algorithm with no priority queue: linear (AVX2/OpenMP-vectorised) min-scan over a compacted swap-removed frontier array of tentative distances, plus CSR out-edge relaxation and a settled-node bitmask.

Anti-diagonal (wavefront) Needleman-Wunsch: per-diagonal SIMD (AVX2/AVX-512) max of diag+score and max(left,up)+gap over three rotating int16 diagonal buffers, with sequence b reversed so both operand streams are contiguous along each anti-diagonal; a two-row scalar NW is used only as an out-of-regime/allocation-failure fallback.

Banded Needleman-Wunsch (band half-width derived from the Hamming distance bound g <= 2D/5) computed as an anti-diagonal wavefront with three rolling diagonals and AVX2 32-bit SIMD lanes, with a two-row scalar DP fallback for small n or wide bands.

Ukkonen-banded anti-diagonal SIMD Needleman-Wunsch, with an O(n) vectorized zero-gap match count plus an exact best-single-gap prefix scan used only as a lower bound to size (or occasionally skip) the band.

Banded anti-diagonal (wavefront) Needleman-Wunsch with AVX2 32-bit lanes, where the band half-width comes from an O(n) prefix/suffix-scan lower bound over all zero- and one-gap alignments (plus a probe-band re-tightening), falling back to two-row NW for small/failed cases

SipHash-style 4x64-bit coupled state: each 32-byte block XORed one word per lane, then two SipRounds of ARX cross-mixing (so every lane becomes a function of all four) with a second cross-lane re-injection of the same words, plus length-seeded IVs, 8-byte tail path, three finalization rounds, XOR-fold of all four lanes and a MurmurHash3 fmix64 tail.

Verbatim xxHash64: four parallel 64-bit accumulators seeded with the standard PRIME64 constants, 32/64-byte striped rounds of acc += w*P2; rotl31; acc *= P1, merged via rotl(1,7,12,18) and mergeRound, plus length, 8/4/1-byte tail rounds, and the standard xor-shift/multiply final avalanche.

Single 64-bit accumulator hash: xor each 8-byte word, then a fixed two ARX rounds of add-constant, xorshift, and RC5-style data-dependent rotation by the accumulator's own low bits (no multiplication), with a length seed, overlapping tail read, and a xor-rotate-add finalizer.

Wide 1024-bit ARX state (16 x 64-bit lanes, pi-digit IVs) absorbing 128-byte blocks by XOR plus a multiply-free Speck128-style rotate-add-xor round with the state chained across blocks (AVX2/OpenMP-parallelised), then BLAKE2b-style column+diagonal G rounds and a one-way 1024->64-bit fold finished by murmur3 fmix64.

Byte/word-at-a-time chained CRC-32C (table-driven software path, _mm_crc32_u64 hardware path) over a two-word rolling state where the previous CRC output seeds the next and the older state word is XORed into the input, finished by a 7-step xorshift-multiply (fmix-style) avalanche finalizer.

Dijkstra's single-source shortest path on a CSR graph with a density switch: SIMD (AVX2) linear-scan argmin over the tentative-distance array (O(n^2)) for dense graphs, and a 4-ary lazy-deletion binary-style heap (O((n+m) log n)) for sparse graphs.
